_README: WAIVER LEDGER — fleet default model ids that are KNOWINGLY shipped without a detection
profile. Enforced by tests/test_fleet_default_screening_floor.py in the required
A model id configured as a fleet default must either resolve to a real profile or appear
here. This file is the ONLY way to ship an unscreened default, and it is deliberately
uncomfortable to use: every entry carries an owner, a reason, what would clear it, and an
EXPIRY. An entry past its expiry FAILS the build — a waiver that never expires is not a
waiver, it is a silent gap that has learned to look official.
An entry is also REMOVED automatically-or-else: the floor fails if an entry names a model
id that is no longer a fleet default, or one that has since acquired a profile. The ledger
cannot accumulate stale rows that hide real coverage.
WHAT THIS FILE IS NOT: it is not a profile, and it contains no thresholds, weights or
feature values. Registering an id here records that we CANNOT screen it. Real detection
parameters come only from a characterisation run (labelled corpus, real model calls,
effect sizes, held-out validation). Inventing them would manufacture exactly the
confident-verdict-from-nothing failure the detector exists to catch.

reason: David's explicit instruction (2026-07-26) is that the fleet defaults to the grok-4.20
pair; a second vendor confirmed against official xAI docs that the alias and pricing
are real and current, so the DEFAULT is correct. What does not exist is a detection
profile for grok version 4.20. ProfileRouter._resolve_grok deliberately returns None
for it rather than borrowing the grok-4 profile, because
"grok-4.20-non-reasoning".startswith("grok-4") is True and the resolver it replaced
was silently scoring 4.20 traffic against a DIFFERENT model's fingerprint. An honest
UNKNOWN beats a borrowed fingerprint, so DetectionEngine returns
why_not_fall_back_to_a_profiled_grok_id: Because it would buy no screening. Every grok id with a CROSS-DOMAIN-VALIDATED profile
is either retired (grok-4-fast-* and the grok-3 family are in RETIRED_MODEL_IDS, so a
default there could not run at all) or is grok-4-1-fast-*, whose profile requires
logprob features that the /detect/verify path cannot supply. MEASURED:
So switching the default to a 'profiled' grok id yields UNKNOWN on this path anyway —
the same unscreened outcome, minus the capability David asked for. grok-4's own profile
records status: provisional, code-domain only, 150/200 prompts before quota exhaustion,
not cross-domain validated; routing to it would be a weak verdict, not a strong one.
The tradeoff was therefore decided in favour of the instructed default plus loud
unscreened-ness, and the loudness is load-bearing.
loudness_that_makes_this_acceptable: 'no_profile_for_model', and a plain-English arkheia_warning naming what would clear
caller, before the call: run_grok's docstring — which is what the MCP client shows the
agent — leads with 'THE DEFAULT MODEL IS NOT SCREENED'
operator log: _log_verdict emits logger.WARNING 'NOT SCREENED (reason=...) — response
ran UNSCORED' instead of a calm INFO line
with the reason in the payload (proxy/endpoints/detect.py::_envelope_risk_band)
operator dashboard: /admin/ui renders Detection reason + What would clear it beside the
UNKNOWN badge, instead of a bare badge with the reason swallowed
what_would_clear_it: A characterisation run for grok-4.20-non-reasoning: labelled TRUTH/FAB corpus, real
model calls against a WORKING xAI key, per-feature effect sizes, held-out validation,
then a profiles/grok-4.20-non-reasoning.yaml. That run is budget-gated workstation work
and is blocked on the xAI key, which currently returns 'Incorrect API key provided' for
every request including GET /v1/language-models. Rotating the key is David's.
not_covered_by_this_entry: grok-4.20-reasoning and grok-4.5 are equally unprofiled but are NOT code defaults, so
the floor does not derive them and they are not waived here. If either is ever made a
default, the floor fails until it is registered.

_FALLBACK_README: The same waiver contract, for the hard-coded profile FALLBACK ids the version routers
reach for via ProfileRouter._by_model_id(). A fallback naming a profile that no file
provides silently falls through, and the crude prefix/family match downstream can then
borrow another version's fingerprint — the same defect class as an unprofiled default,

reason: FOUND BY THIS FLOOR ON ITS FIRST RUN, not by review. _resolve_recent_gpt routes any
'5.2-codex' or '5.3-codex' id to _by_model_id('gpt-5.2-codex'), but NO loaded profile
has that id — because profiles/gpt-5.2-codex.yaml declares `model: "gpt-5-codex"`,
the SAME id as profiles/gpt-5-codex.yaml. ProfileRouter.load_all keys its dict by the
declared model id, so the two files collide and one is silently discarded by glob
order. MEASURED: the surviving profile is version 3.0 (gpt-5-codex.yaml), so the v4.0
content of gpt-5.2-codex.yaml is DEAD — loaded, keyed over, never used.
and get() falls through to the crude prefix match, which lands on gpt-5-codex v3.0.
why_not_fixed_here: Both candidate fixes CHANGE DETECTION BEHAVIOUR for live traffic on evidence I do not
have. Renaming gpt-5.2-codex.yaml's `model:` field would ACTIVATE an unvalidated v4.0
profile for gpt-5.2/5.3-codex traffic; repointing the router literal would pin a
cross-version borrow as deliberate. Which profile legitimately characterises
gpt-5.2-codex is a characterisation-owner decision, and guessing it is the same class
of error as inventing thresholds. Reported, waived with a short expiry, not papered
over. Load-time collision detection was added so the discard is no longer silent.
what_would_clear_it: Decide which file characterises gpt-5.2-codex, give it that model id (so the two files
stop colliding), and confirm router.get('gpt-5.2-codex') resolves to it. If the answer
is that gpt-5.2-codex should legitimately share the gpt-5-codex surface, delete the
duplicate file and change the router literal to gpt-5-codex so the intent is explicit
